summary: All four RHEL 9 nodes now meet the rsyslog standard and remain healthy after sequential reboots. TCP 5514 accepts local0 messages into /var/log/infraset-app.log. SELinux and firewalld policies persist, rsyslog is enabled, and every records.db checksum is unchanged.
actions_performed: Verified the installed rsyslog RPM and package integrity.
Installed an identical validated rsyslog drop-in on all nodes for imtcp port 5514 and local0 logging.
Enabled and started rsyslog on every node.
Persistently labeled TCP 5514 as syslogd_port_t and allowed it through the active firewalld zone.
Corrected node1's drifted destination-log SELinux context from tmp_t to var_log_t.
Proved ingestion by sending local0 messages to each node's managed IP on TCP 5514.
Restarted node1 through node4 one at a time and verified changed boot identities and complete recovery.

evidence.requirement: Package, configuration, service, TCP ingestion, and current health on all nodes
evidence.summary: Final per-node checks show a clean rsyslog RPM, valid identical configuration, enabled/active service, TCP 5514 listener, and successful local0 delivery to the required file.
After reboot, SELinux is enforcing with TCP 5514 assigned to syslogd_port_t; firewalld is active and allows 5514/tcp in both runtime and permanent state.

evidence.requirement: Application data preserved on every node
evidence.summary: Initial and final SHA-256 digests of /var/lib/infraset-app/data/records.db match individually on all four nodes.
Healthy baseline, acknowledged safe reboot, changed boot ID, and recovered service/security/data plus post-reboot TCP delivery.
